t: That this Act may be cited as the “Natural Gas Pipeline Safety Act of 1968”.

fable.w: This section is only a short-title provision naming the Act. It sets up no decision process, consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The tempting reading is that a pipeline safety act must involve regulation and industry or state input, but nothing of that kind appears in this section's text.
fable.s: That this Act may be cited as the “Natural Gas Pipeline Safety Act of 1968”.

opus.w: This section only gives the Act's short title. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Other parts of the Act may provide for rulemaking or advisory committees, but this clause has no participation process, so the answer is No.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** The tempting reading is that the Natural Gas Pipeline Safety Act of 1968 includes rulemaking and advisory committees, which would count as participation. That fails because this SECTION is only the short-title clause. It contains no decision process and involves no outside party. Under the DEFINITION, a section's text must itself provide for participation.
